0|d821a4c4d11ad160925dab2bb009b8444beff484|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"e1000e: DoS while TSO enabled caused by link partner with small MSS
With a low enough MSS on the link partner and TSO enabled locally
networking stack can periodically send a very large (e.g.  64KB) TCP
message for which the driver will attempt to use more Tx descriptors than
are available by default in the Tx ring.  This is due to a workaround in
the code that imposes a limit of only 4 MSS-sized segments per descriptor
which appears to be a carry-over from the older e1000 driver and may be
applicable only to some older PCI or PCIx parts which are not supported in
e1000e.  When the driver gets a message that is too large to fit across the
configured number of Tx descriptors
column2: it stops the upper stack from queueing

column1: any more and gets stuck in this state.  After a timeout
assumes the adapter is hung and calls the driver to reset it.
Remove the unnecessary limitation of using up to only 4 MSS-sized segments
per Tx descriptor
column2: and put in a hard failure test to catch when attempting

column1: to check for message sizes larger than would fit in the whole Tx ring.
Refactor the remaining logic that limits the size of data per Tx descriptor
from a seemingly arbitrary 8KB to a limit based on the dynamic size of the
Tx packet buffer as described in the hardware specification.
Also
column2: fix the logic in the check for space in the Tx ring for the next

column1: largest possible packet after the current one has been successfully queued
for transmit
column2: and use the appropriate defines for default ring sizes in

column1: e1000_probe instead of magic values.
This issue goes back to the introduction of e1000e in 2.6.24 when it was
split off from e1000.
